user_story: As a maintainer, I want the decision model behind a provider-agnostic seam so that the gate is not welded to one vendor and the repo keeps working with no SDK installed.
acceptance_criteria: A protocol with `evaluate(state, questions) -> DecisionResult` and `close()`; `DecisionResult.values` is a probability per question id, documented as "probability the predicate is true, not confidence in a label"; importing `task_master` and `mcp_server` still works with no third-party package present.
traces_to: ELI5 "a model rather than a regex"; foreman `base.py`

user_story: As a maintainer, I want a Jev adapter using the official SDK so that the gate asks real questions of a real System One model.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter calls `system_one(state=…, questions={id: Noul(instructions=…)}, model, timeout)`; reads each answer from `response.nouls[id].noul` with a Mapping fallback; clamps finite values into `[0, 1]`; raises a typed error when the SDK is absent rather than crashing on import.

user_story: As an agent closing a row, I want the state sent to the model to be assembled from the repo so that the judgement is about what was actually built.
acceptance_criteria: State carries the row's acceptance criteria verbatim, the diff that claims to implement them, and the artifacts the validation doc names (test path, newman collection, review notes); every path is resolved under the project root; a missing artifact is reported as missing, not silently omitted.
traces_to: README "handed the row's acceptance criteria, the diff … and the test"

user_story: As a maintainer, I want one Noul question per acceptance criterion so that the answer says which criterion is unaddressed rather than giving one blurred score.
acceptance_criteria: A row with N criteria produces N named questions in a single call; the result maps criterion -> probability; the unaddressed ones are listed individually in the output.

user_story: As an agent, I want a `task_assess` MCP tool and a `task-master assess` CLI command so that the check is available to both the human and the no-human-in-the-loop workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Both run the same code path and print the same verdict: per-criterion probability, the overall decision, and the threshold it was compared against; the MCP tool's description states that the result is a probability and not a proof.
traces_to: README "one more tool on this same server, `task_assess(id)`"

user_story: As a reviewer, I want `done` to consult the assessment as well as the paperwork so that a truthful-looking validation doc about the wrong behaviour does not close a row.
acceptance_criteria: With the gate enabled, `set_status(done)` requires both a PASS validation doc and an assessment at or above the threshold; the refusal names which of the two failed.

user_story: As a developer, I want a below-threshold assessment to park the row rather than fail the run so that an uncertain verdict produces a hand-off instead of a blocked build.
acceptance_criteria: A low or `covers: false` result sets the row `blocked` with the unaddressed criteria in its notes, and exits non-zero without touching any other row.
traces_to: ELI5 "doesn't fail the build — it parks the row"

user_story: As a maintainer, I want the semantic gate off unless it is configured so that this stays a standard-library tool for everyone who does not want it.
acceptance_criteria: With no provider configured, every command behaves exactly as it does today and no network call is attempted; enabling it is one setting, and the setting plus the threshold are both documented.
traces_to: README "Python 3 standard library only"; CCAR-F "process gate, not a necessity"

user_story: As a maintainer, I want a missing key, a timeout or a malformed response to fail closed and loudly so that the gate never invents a score.
acceptance_criteria: Each failure raises a typed error naming the cause, no probability is fabricated or defaulted, and the row's status is left unchanged; a timeout is bounded by an explicit, configurable deadline.
traces_to: foreman "no score is invented for a refusal"

user_story: As a reviewer six months later, I want the assessment recorded on the row so that I can see what the model actually said when it was closed.
acceptance_criteria: The row keeps the score, the threshold it was compared against, the provider and model id, and the date; the value is visible in `show` and survives a rewrite of the CSV.

user_story: As a contributor, I want the whole gate testable with no API key so that the suite runs offline and in CI.
acceptance_criteria: A stub adapter returns scripted probabilities; tests cover a pass, a below-threshold park, a malformed response, an absent SDK and a timeout; the suite runs with one documented command and needs no credentials.
notes: tests written, red until decision_model.py and assess.py exist

user_story: As a reader of the docs, I want the documented return shape to match what the model actually returns so that the design notes stop describing an interface that does not exist.
acceptance_criteria: README and ELI5-MCP no longer claim `{"covers": true, "confidence": 0.93}`; both describe a probability per criterion, say the probability needs calibration per project, and keep the "typed does not prove the semantic judgement" caveat.
traces_to: foreman "typed means the response shape is constrained"

user_story: As a user of a scaffolded project, I want the validation format to carry the assessment so that every project inheriting these templates gets the same audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: `templates/validation.README.md` documents the assessment line, an existing doc without one still validates, and a scaffolded project needs no edit to keep working.
